newsitem.title: FRANCE: Seita says being sued by cancer-hit smoker.
newsitem.headline: Seita says being sued by cancer-hit smoker.

text.p: French tobacco company Seita said on Thursday it was being sued by a cancer-stricken smoker who blamed his illness on consumption of its cigarettes in the first legal case of its type in France.
Seita said there was no legal substance to the plaintiff's allegations and said it was confident about the outcome of the court case.
It said that the smoker was seeking damages linked to what he alleged was a lack of information about the risks linked to the consumption of tobacco.
The smoker attributes his cancer to smoking Seita's famous pungent Gauloises Brunes cigarettes, Seita said.

Seita said that the only similar legal proceedings ever undertaken in France were brought against a bank by the family of an employee who claimed that she had been the victim of passive smoking. A Paris district court threw out the case on November 20, 1996 on the basis of a lack of legal grounds.
It noted that there had been other cases of this kind outside France, notably in the United States, but that no such proceedings had led to damage payments of any kind.
"As for the case brought against Seita, the company considers that there are no serious legal grounds and it is confident about the outcome of the proceedings," it said.
